text:
Emma P.: Thanks everyone — quick post-allhands follow-up. Dropping a short FAQ and open thread for any leftover career/comp/benefits questions. I’ll answer in-thread or follow up 1:1 when needed. :handshake:

Jordan L.: Thanks! can you confirm promo effective date for the next cycle? is it the end of the month or start of next pay period?

Emma P.: Good q — promotions approved in this cycle will be effective the first day of the following pay period (so salary change shows on next paycheck). Exceptions require exec sign-off and payroll lead time.

Micah R.: If my manager says they're putting forward a recommendation now but calibration is later, should I expect comp change to be retroactive?

Emma P.: Generally we don’t do retroactive base changes except in cases of system error. If a comp correction is needed we’ll handle on a case-by-case basis and coordinate with payroll. Please ping me or @people-ops-bot with the ticket.

Olivia K.: Quick ask on leveling evidence — what template do managers prefer? Ours felt a bit vague during the all-hands.

Raj S.: echoing Olivia — would love a short checklist (impact, scope, mentoring, cross-team influence).

Emma P.: Good call. We’ll publish a 1-page checklist: Impact examples, scope laddering, cross-functional evidence, and suggested artifacts (PRs, OKR contributions, customer notes). Will post in #docs and link here when live.

Sofia M.: Any guidance for out-of-cycle promo/bump requests for hiring/retention reasons? Is there a budget guardrail?

Jordan L.: For context, hiring market stuff — curious how tight the window is for approving retention increases.

Emma P.: Out-of-cycle increases are allowed but require a manager + director justification and People Ops approval; they route through a retention budget pool. Typical approval takes 7–10 business days. If urgent (offer counter / critical role) mark as high-priority and include comp rationale + market data.

Micah R.: Are equity refreshes tied to promo cycles or separate?

Emma P.: Refresh timing is separate and depends on role/tenure. Managers will coordinate with People Ops; refreshes are not guaranteed at promotion.

Olivia K.: Benefits Q: any update on parental leave top-up policy? someone mentioned changes in the all-hands slide but I missed details.

Emma P.: We’re piloting a 6-week top-up for primary caregivers for hires before July 1. Pilot details + eligibility posted next week. If you want to opt in to the pilot feedback group DM me.

Raj S.: 401k match timing question — when does new-match contribution show in statements after enrollment?

Emma P.: Matches are applied each pay period; first match shows on the next payroll cycle after your enrollment processes (usually 1 pay period). We’ll confirm timing on the enrollment doc.

Sofia M.: Calibration timeline: when will managers get the normalized scores? we need to prep calibration notes.

Emma P.: Managers will receive normalized calibration packets two business days before calibration meetings. If you don't see yours by then, escalate to your lead or ping me.

Jordan L.: Is there an appeals window after calibration if a manager thinks a slot was missed?

Emma P.: Yes — there’s a short appeals window (5 business days) post-calibration to submit additional evidence. People Ops + Comp will review.

Micah R.: tiny thing — will comp band ranges be public to managers only or to ICs too? asking for transparency.

Emma P.: We’re keeping band ranges visible to managers and recruitment partners. We’re evaluating broader transparency and will share our thinking once leadership finalizes.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: link to current comp & leveling decks -> https://intranet.redwood/career/comp-leveling (internal only) :link:

Olivia K.: thanks — appreciate the follow-up. I’ll wait for the checklist link.

Emma P.: Thanks all — I’ll update this thread when the checklist, pilot docs, and comp packet links are up. If you need private help, DM me or schedule a 1:1. :slightly_smiling_face:
